evidence_priority: official marking intention and mark allocation
equivalent_answer_policy: Award the same marks for code with equivalent behaviour and constraints.
Do not require cosmetic agreement with the model solution.
When a method is explicitly requested, that method remains part of the assessment.
Do not silently repair or change code before tracing it.
Use safe current practice in model solutions while recognising lecture-aligned alternatives.

question_bank.title: Internet, intranet and extranet
question_bank.question: Define Internet, intranet and extranet.
question_bank.model_answer: Internet: the global network of interconnected networks. Intranet: a private organisational network using Internet standards for authorised users. Extranet: controlled access that extends selected intranet resources to authorised external parties.
question_bank.acceptable_alternatives: Equivalent wording is accepted when the access scope and purpose are accurate.

question_bank.title: Web versus Internet
question_bank.question: Differentiate the Web from the Internet and state which one provides the infrastructure for the other.
question_bank.model_answer: The Internet is the global network infrastructure. The Web is an information-sharing system of linked resources accessed over that infrastructure. The Internet provides the infrastructure for the Web.

rubric.criterion: Web described as an information/resource system

question_bank.title: HTTP request and response
question_bank.question: Explain the HTTP request-response cycle when a browser retrieves a page, including one successful status code and one client-error status code.
question_bank.model_answer: The browser sends an HTTP request to the web server. The server locates or generates the resource and returns an HTTP response containing a status code, headers and usually a body. 200 means success; 404 means the requested resource was not found.
question_bank.acceptable_alternatives: Any accurate 2xx success and 4xx client-error examples are accepted.

question_bank.title: Browser and server roles
question_bank.question: Compare a web browser and a web server using their role, location of execution and one example of each.
question_bank.model_answer: A browser is client software that requests resources and renders HTML/CSS while executing client-side JavaScript, for example Chrome or Firefox. A web server receives HTTP requests and returns static or generated responses, for example Apache or Nginx.

question_bank.title: Select a web platform
question_bank.question: A faculty needs a site that non-programmers can update, supports role-based publishing, and can be accessed from standard browsers. Recommend an appropriate platform category and explain four relevant characteristics.
question_bank.model_answer: Recommend a content management system. Relevant characteristics include browser-based administration, reusable themes/templates, user roles and permissions, content workflow/versioning, extensions/plugins, and centralised publishing.
question_bank.acceptable_alternatives: Any four accurate CMS characteristics connected to the scenario are accepted. Named CMS products may be examples but do not replace the explanation.

question_bank.title: HTML document structure
question_bank.question: Write the minimum valid HTML5 structure for a page titled ICT600 that displays a level-one heading reading Web Technology.
question_bank.model_answer: A valid answer contains the HTML5 doctype, html, head, title, body and h1 elements with correct nesting and closing tags.

rubric.criterion: Correct h1 content and valid nesting

question_bank.answer_code: Web Technology

question_bank.title: Accessible linked image
question_bank.question: Write HTML that displays uitmlogo.jpg with alternative text UiTM Logo and makes the image link to https://www.uitm.edu.my/.
question_bank.model_answer: Use a valid img element inside an anchor element. The alt attribute must describe the image.

rubric.criterion: Valid nesting and ASCII quotation marks

question_bank.correction_note: The historical scheme used smart/missing quotation marks and was not valid HTML.

question_bank.title: Internal and external CSS
question_bank.question: Explain internal and external CSS. Give one valid code example of each and one situation where each is appropriate.
question_bank.model_answer: Internal CSS is placed in a style element in the document head and is useful for a single page. External CSS is stored in a separate .css file and linked with a link element; it is preferable for consistent styling across multiple pages.
question_bank.correction_note: Use CSS comments /* ... */ when annotations are included; // is not valid CSS comment syntax.
question_bank.answer_code:
<!-- Internal -->
<style>h1 { color: navy; }</style>

<!-- External -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">

question_bank.title: Semantic POST form
question_bank.question: Construct an HTML form that posts to register.php and collects full name, email, programme and password. All fields are required; email and password must use suitable input types; include an associated label for every control and a submit button.
question_bank.model_answer: The form uses method=post and action=register.php, labelled controls with name attributes, required validation, correct email/password types and a submit control.

rubric.criterion: Email and password use suitable types

question_bank.acceptable_alternatives: A select element or text input may collect programme. Different ids and names are accepted when internally consistent.
question_bank.answer_code:
<form method="post" action="register.php">
  <label for="fullName">Full name</label>
  <input id="fullName" name="fullName" required>
  <label for="email">Email</label>
  <input id="email" name="email" type="email" required>
  <label for="programme">Programme</label>
  <input id="programme" name="programme" required>
  <label for="password">Password</label>
  <input id="password" name="password" type="password" required>
  <button type="submit">Register</button>
</form>

question_bank.title: Responsive page decision
question_bank.question: A two-column desktop page becomes unreadable on a phone. Propose an eight-mark CSS-based correction that follows responsive web design principles.
question_bank.model_answer: Use a mobile-friendly viewport, flexible dimensions, a layout mechanism such as grid/flexbox, and a media query that collapses the columns. Images should not exceed their container.

rubric.criterion: Media query with a suitable breakpoint

question_bank.acceptable_alternatives: Grid or flexbox is accepted. A different reasonable breakpoint is accepted.
question_bank.answer_code:
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<style>
.layout { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 2fr 1fr; gap: 1rem; }
img { max-width: 100%; height: auto; }
@media (max-width: 700px) {
  .layout { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
}
</style>

question_bank.title: JavaScript inclusion and loading
question_bank.question: List three ways to include JavaScript in an HTML document and explain one non-blocking way to load an external script.
question_bank.model_answer: JavaScript may be inline in an event attribute, internal in a script element, or external in a .js file referenced by src. An external script in the head with defer downloads without blocking parsing and executes after the document is parsed.
question_bank.correction_note: Bottom-of-body placement is valid, but it is not the only modern recommendation.
question_bank.answer_code: <script src="app.js" defer></script>

question_bank.title: DOM content update
question_bank.question: Write JavaScript that reads a value from an input with id studentName and displays Welcome, followed by that name, in an element with id result when a button with id greet is clicked.
question_bank.model_answer: Retrieve the elements, register a click handler, read the input value and update the result. textContent is preferred because the output is plain text.
question_bank.acceptable_alternatives: querySelector or getElementById; function declaration, anonymous callback or arrow function; textContent or innerHTML are accepted when used safely.

question_bank.title: Explicit-rate currency function
question_bank.question: Create a JavaScript function convertUsdToMyr(usd, rate) that returns the converted value. Using the explicitly supplied rate 1 USD = MYR 4.34, display the conversion of USD 25 to two decimal places.
question_bank.model_answer: Multiply usd by rate, return the result and format the displayed value to two decimal places. USD 25 is MYR 108.50 at the stated rate.
question_bank.correction_note: The historical question omitted the exchange rate while its scheme assumed one.

question_bank.title: Form validation
question_bank.question: Write JavaScript for a form with id signupForm that prevents submission when the email field is empty or the age is not an integer from 18 to 60. Display one clear message in an element with id error.
question_bank.model_answer: Handle submit, read and trim the email, convert age to a number, validate both conditions, prevent submission only when invalid, and display an appropriate message.

rubric.criterion: Valid data is allowed to submit

question_bank.acceptable_alternatives: Equivalent Boolean logic and DOM-selection methods are accepted. Built-in HTML validation may supplement but not replace the requested JavaScript checks.

question_bank.title: Average and result category
question_bank.question: Develop calculateAverage(a, b, c). It must return the average of three numeric scores. Display the average and PASS when it is at least 50; otherwise display FAIL.
question_bank.model_answer: Add the scores, divide by three, return the average, apply the threshold and display both values.
question_bank.acceptable_alternatives: A function declaration or arrow function is accepted. DOM output or console output is accepted only if the question implementation context identifies that destination.

question_bank.title: PHP scalar data types
question_bank.question: List the four PHP scalar data types and give one literal example of each.
question_bank.model_answer: Boolean (true), integer (25), float/double (3.5), and string ('ICT600').

question_bank.title: Exact PHP string trace
question_bank.question: Produce the exact output of the supplied PHP statements. Do not silently change the source string or search terms.
question_bank.model_answer: The replacement leaves the sentence unchanged because can is absent. substr($text, 2, 6) returns e sell. strpos($text, 'can') returns bool(false).

rubric.criterion: Reasoning recognises that can is absent

question_bank.correction_note: The historical scheme changed the operations and therefore answered a different program.
question_bank.answer_code:
She sells sea shells by the sea shore now
e sell
bool(false)

question_bank.title: Function requirement fidelity
question_bank.question: Write a PHP function printFirstName($firstName, $lastName) that accepts two parameters but prints only the first parameter. Call it using Aina and Rahman.
question_bank.model_answer: The function has two parameters, valid braces, echoes only $firstName, and is called with both values.
question_bank.correction_note: The historical answer omitted an opening brace and printed both parameters.

question_bank.title: Array to table
question_bank.question: Using a PHP multidimensional array, store and display these rows in an HTML table: ICT600, Web Technology, 3; ICT602, Mobile Technology, 3.
question_bank.model_answer: Create a nested array and iterate or index it to output two valid table rows and three cells per row.
question_bank.acceptable_alternatives: A foreach loop or explicit array indexes are accepted. Associative or indexed nested arrays are accepted.

question_bank.title: Safe POST processing
question_bank.question: Develop receive.php to read name and programme from a POST request. Reject an empty value and otherwise display both values safely in HTML.
question_bank.model_answer: Require the POST method, read values with defaults, trim them, reject missing input, encode untrusted output and display the accepted values.
question_bank.acceptable_alternatives: filter_input may replace direct $_POST access. A helper function may encode output. Equivalent validation structure is accepted.
question_bank.answer_code:
Name:

Programme:

question_bank.title: HTTP statelessness and state
question_bank.question: Explain why HTTP is described as stateless and distinguish how a cookie and a server-side session can maintain state.
question_bank.model_answer: HTTP treats each request independently. A cookie stores a small value in the browser and sends applicable values with later requests. A server-side session stores state on the server and normally identifies the session through a cookie containing a session identifier.

question_bank.title: GET, POST and HTTPS
question_bank.question: Differentiate GET and POST by data location and typical purpose. Explain why POST alone does not make a password confidential.
question_bank.model_answer: GET parameters are commonly placed in the URL query string and suit retrieval. POST sends data in the request body and suits submissions or state changes. POST is not encryption; HTTPS/TLS is required to protect data in transit.
question_bank.source_basis: Corrected from the undated Test 1 answer-only scheme
question_bank.correction_note: The historical explanation could be read as if POST itself protects sensitive information.

question_bank.title: HTTP status-code diagnosis
question_bank.question: For each situation, state the most suitable HTTP status code: successful retrieval; missing page; unauthenticated request; authenticated user lacks permission; server-side failure; malformed client request.
question_bank.acceptable_alternatives: Accept another precise 2xx success code only when justified by a changed scenario; otherwise use the listed codes.

question_bank.title: PHP session lifecycle
question_bank.question: Write PHP that starts a session, stores the logged-in username Aina, reads it on the same request and provides a logout branch that clears the session when ?logout=1 is supplied.
question_bank.model_answer: Start the session before output, assign and read a session value, and on logout clear data and destroy the session.
question_bank.acceptable_alternatives: Explicitly unsetting the username may replace session_unset when the requirement is limited to that key.
question_bank.answer_code:
<?php
session_start();
if (($_GET['logout'] ?? '') === '1') {
    session_unset();
    session_destroy();
    exit('Logged out');
}
$_SESSION['username'] = 'Aina';
echo htmlspecialchars($_SESSION['username'], ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8');
?>

question_bank.title: AJAX interaction
question_bank.question: Explain the AJAX request flow for a live-search box and give two advantages and one limitation of using AJAX for this feature.
question_bank.model_answer: A user event triggers JavaScript, which sends an asynchronous HTTP request. The server processes the query and returns data; JavaScript updates part of the page without a full reload. Advantages include responsiveness and reduced full-page transfer. Limitations include added client-side complexity, error handling, accessibility/history concerns, or dependency on JavaScript/network availability.

rubric.criterion: Event, request, server response and partial DOM update

question_bank.acceptable_alternatives: fetch, XMLHttpRequest, JSON or XML terminology is accepted when the described flow is correct.

question_bank.title: Database terminology
question_bank.question: Define database, DBMS and database system (DBS).
question_bank.model_answer: A database is an organised collection of data. A DBMS is software used to create, maintain and access databases. A database system consists of the database, DBMS and supporting tools/interfaces.

question_bank.title: Relational table design
question_bank.question: Write MySQL DDL for a students table with student_id as an automatically incrementing primary key, name up to 100 characters, unique email up to 150 characters, and cgpa with two decimal places.
question_bank.model_answer: Use CREATE TABLE, suitable data types, AUTO_INCREMENT, PRIMARY KEY and UNIQUE constraints.
question_bank.correction_note: AUTO_INCREMENT is required when the question or rubric specifies automatic identifiers.

question_bank.title: CRUD statements
question_bank.question: For a courses(code, title, credit) table, write one SQL statement each to insert ICT600/Web Technology/3, update its credit to 4, select the row, and delete the row.
question_bank.model_answer: Use INSERT, UPDATE with WHERE, SELECT with WHERE, and DELETE with WHERE.

question_bank.title: Related-table query
question_bank.question: Tables students(student_id, name) and registrations(student_id, course_code, mark) are related by student_id. Write SQL to list each student's name and mark for ICT600, highest mark first.
question_bank.model_answer: Join students to registrations on student_id, filter ICT600, select name and mark, and sort mark descending.
question_bank.acceptable_alternatives: INNER JOIN or an equivalent valid join expression is accepted. Table aliases are optional.
question_bank.answer_code:
SELECT s.name, r.mark
FROM students AS s
INNER JOIN registrations AS r
  ON s.student_id = r.student_id
WHERE r.course_code = 'ICT600'
ORDER BY r.mark DESC;

question_bank.title: Prepared MySQLi insert
question_bank.question: Using an existing MySQLi connection $conn, write PHP that reads name and email from POST, rejects empty values, and inserts them into students(name, email) with a prepared statement.
question_bank.model_answer: Read and validate both values, prepare an INSERT with placeholders, bind two strings, execute it and handle success/failure.
question_bank.acceptable_alternatives: PDO with named or positional parameters is fully accepted. Procedural or object-oriented MySQLi is accepted. Direct interpolation is not equivalent because it omits the requested prepared statement.
question_bank.answer_code:
<?php
$name = trim($_POST['name'] ?? '');
$email = trim($_POST['email'] ?? '');
if ($name === '' || $email === '') {
    exit('Name and email are required.');
}
$stmt = mysqli_prepare($conn,
    'INSERT INTO students (name, email) VALUES (?, ?)');
mysqli_stmt_bind_param($stmt, 'ss', $name, $email);
echo mysqli_stmt_execute($stmt) ? 'Saved' : 'Insert failed';
mysqli_stmt_close($stmt);
?>

question_bank.title: Web application framework
question_bank.question: Define a web application framework and state two problems it commonly reduces.
question_bank.model_answer: A web application framework is a reusable collection of libraries, conventions and tools that supports web application development. It reduces repeated infrastructure work and encourages organised, maintainable code.

question_bank.title: MVC responsibilities
question_bank.question: Explain the responsibility of the Model, View and Controller in MVC.
question_bank.model_answer: The Model represents data and business/data-access logic. The View presents information to the user. The Controller receives requests/input, coordinates processing with the Model and selects a response/View.
question_bank.acceptable_alternatives: Wording may follow the lecture notes or a named MVC framework, provided responsibilities are separated correctly.

question_bank.title: MVC request flow
question_bank.question: A user requests /courses/ICT600. Sequence the request through a router, controller, model and view, and identify the data passed between them.
question_bank.model_answer: The router matches the URL to a controller action. The controller requests ICT600 data from the Model. The Model reads/returns course data. The controller passes that data to the View. The View renders the response returned to the user.

rubric.criterion: Controller to model with requested identifier

question_bank.title: Framework trade-offs
question_bank.question: Assess two advantages and two disadvantages of using a framework for a medium-sized team web application.
question_bank.model_answer: Advantages include reusable components, standard structure, faster development, routing/database/security facilities and easier teamwork. Disadvantages include learning curve, framework overhead, version dependency, reduced flexibility and vulnerabilities in outdated framework code.
question_bank.acceptable_alternatives: Any well-explained advantages/disadvantages consistent with the lecture notes are accepted.

question_bank.title: Map code to MVC
question_bank.question: Design the MVC responsibilities for a student-list page. State what belongs in the Model, View and Controller, and explain two benefits of this separation.
question_bank.model_answer: Model: retrieve and represent student records. Controller: handle the request, call the Model and pass records to the View. View: render the student table without database access. Benefits include maintainability, testability, reusability, parallel team work and easier changes to presentation/data storage.

question_bank.title: Web application versus web service
question_bank.question: Differentiate a web application from a web service using the primary consumer and interface.
question_bank.model_answer: A web application normally provides a user interface for people. A web service exposes a programmatic interface so software systems can exchange data or invoke functionality.

question_bank.title: SOAP platform components
question_bank.question: Explain the role of XML, SOAP, WSDL and UDDI in the traditional web-services platform.
question_bank.model_answer: XML represents/tags data. SOAP defines the message format used to exchange messages. WSDL describes the service interface and how to access it. UDDI is a registry concept for publishing and discovering services.
question_bank.correction_note: Treat UDDI as the traditional registry model taught in the notes, not as a requirement of every current service.

question_bank.title: RESTful resource operations
question_bank.question: For a RESTful /students resource, map list, retrieve one, create, update and delete operations to suitable HTTP methods and paths.
question_bank.model_answer: GET /students lists; GET /students/15 retrieves one; POST /students creates; PUT or PATCH /students/15 updates; DELETE /students/15 deletes.
question_bank.acceptable_alternatives: PUT or PATCH is accepted for update when used consistently with the stated replacement/partial-update semantics.

question_bank.title: Service provider, requestor and registry
question_bank.question: Describe the roles of service provider, service requestor/consumer and service registry in a traditional web-service architecture.
question_bank.model_answer: The provider implements and publishes the service. The registry stores descriptions to support discovery. The requestor discovers/obtains the description and invokes the provider.

question_bank.title: Choose SOAP or REST
question_bank.question: A mobile application needs a simple JSON API over HTTP. A separate inter-agency system requires a strict XML contract and message-level standards. Recommend REST or SOAP for each and justify the decisions using four characteristics.
question_bank.model_answer: Use REST for the mobile JSON API because it uses resource-oriented HTTP operations and lightweight representations. Use SOAP for the inter-agency system when a formal XML message contract and SOAP-related standards are required.
question_bank.acceptable_alternatives: A different recommendation can receive credit only when it is technically coherent and explicitly connected to the requirements.

question_bank.title: Threat and vulnerability
question_bank.question: Differentiate a threat from a vulnerability and give one web-application example of each.
question_bank.model_answer: A vulnerability is a weakness, such as unvalidated input. A threat is something capable of exploiting a weakness, such as an attacker attempting SQL injection.

question_bank.title: Malware identification
question_bank.question: Identify the most suitable term for each description: self-replicates across systems; appears useful but hides malicious behaviour; encrypts files for payment; secretly collects user information; displays unwanted advertising; infects or modifies other files.
question_bank.model_answer: Worm, Trojan horse, ransomware, spyware, adware, virus.

question_bank.title: SQL injection prevention
question_bank.question: A login query is built by concatenating username and password into SQL. Identify the vulnerability and propose four concrete corrections.
question_bank.model_answer: The vulnerability is SQL injection. Use prepared statements/parameter binding; validate input; store password hashes and verify them with password_verify rather than comparing plain text; use a least-privileged database account; return generic authentication errors.

rubric.criterion: Generic error or other valid defence-in-depth control

question_bank.acceptable_alternatives: Award other concrete defence-in-depth controls, but escaping alone is not equivalent to the requested primary prepared-statement control.

question_bank.title: Cross-site scripting prevention
question_bank.question: A comment entered by a user is inserted into an HTML page without encoding. Identify the vulnerability and show a safe PHP output statement for $comment. Explain why input validation alone is insufficient.
question_bank.model_answer: The vulnerability is cross-site scripting (XSS). Encode untrusted output for the HTML context with htmlspecialchars. Input validation can reject known bad forms but output encoding prevents data from being interpreted as markup/script in its destination context.

rubric.criterion: Why contextual output encoding is still required

question_bank.answer_code: echo htmlspecialchars($comment, ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8');

question_bank.title: Secure session and authentication review
question_bank.question: A site uses HTTP for login, stores plain-text passwords, keeps the same session ID after login, places the session ID in the URL, and never expires sessions. Identify and correct each weakness.
question_bank.model_answer: Use HTTPS/TLS; store passwords with password_hash and verify with password_verify; regenerate the session ID after authentication; keep session identifiers in cookies rather than URLs and set Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite as appropriate; enforce inactivity and absolute timeouts and destroy the session on logout.

rubric.criterion: HTTPS/TLS plus password hashing and verification (2 marks each)
Session ID regeneration plus removal from URLs (2 marks each)
Secure cookie attributes plus timeout/logout controls (2 marks each)

parts.answer: Examples: HTTPS, regenerate ID after login, Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite cookies, inactivity timeout, logout destruction, do not place IDs in URLs.

parts.answer: Use a CMS. A relevant feature may be browser-based editing, roles/workflow, templates/themes or extensions.

parts.question: Rewrite the supplied fragment as valid accessible HTML.
parts.answer: Close the h1 correctly and use valid quoted src/alt attributes.

parts.label: 2(b)
parts.question: Write internal CSS for .notice with a navy background, white text, 1rem padding and centred text.
parts.answer: Use a valid .notice rule with all four declarations.

parts.label: 2(c)
parts.question: Write a form that posts a required email value to register.php. Include an associated label and submit button.
parts.answer: Use POST/action, label for/id, email input with name/required and a submit button.
parts.answer_code:
<form method="post" action="register.php">
  <label for="email">Email</label>
  <input id="email" name="email" type="email" required>
  <button type="submit">Register</button>
</form>

parts.label: 3(a)
parts.question: List three JavaScript inclusion methods and explain why defer can be used for an external script in the head.
parts.answer: Inline, internal and external; defer avoids blocking parsing and runs the script after the document is parsed.

parts.label: 3(b)
parts.question: Write calculateTotal(price, quantity). It must return price multiplied by quantity. When button #calculate is clicked, read numeric inputs #price and #quantity and display Total: RM followed by two decimals in #receipt.
parts.answer: Create the function, handle click, convert inputs to numbers, calculate and update the DOM with two-decimal output.
parts.alternatives: Equivalent DOM selectors and function/callback forms are accepted. innerHTML is accepted if no untrusted markup is inserted.

parts.label: 4(a)
parts.question: Produce the exact output of the PHP code.
parts.answer: Web Technology; bool(false). The replacement term is absent, and strpos returns false.

parts.label: 4(b)
parts.question: Write a PHP function result($mark) returning A for 80+, B for 70-79, C for 60-69 and F below 60. Display the result for 75.
parts.answer: Use a parameter, correctly ordered conditions, return all categories and call with 75 to display B.
parts.alternatives: if/elseif, match or another equivalent valid control structure is accepted.

parts.label: 5(a)
parts.question: Explain stateless HTTP and state one role of a cookie and one role of a session.
parts.answer: Requests are independent; a cookie stores client-side values; a session stores server-side state linked to a client/session identifier.

parts.label: 5(b)
parts.question: State two benefits of AJAX for live search.
parts.answer: Any two: partial update, responsiveness, reduced full-page transfer, asynchronous interaction.

parts.label: 6(a)
parts.question: Write MySQL DDL for courses with course_id as AUTO_INCREMENT primary key, code VARCHAR(10) UNIQUE and title VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL.
parts.answer: Use CREATE TABLE and all stated constraints.

parts.label: 6(b)
parts.question: students(student_id,name) and registrations(student_id,course_code,mark) are related. Write SQL to list name and mark for ICT600, highest mark first.
parts.answer: Join by student_id, filter ICT600 and order by mark descending.
parts.answer_code:
SELECT s.name, r.mark
FROM students s
JOIN registrations r ON r.student_id = s.student_id
WHERE r.course_code = 'ICT600'
ORDER BY r.mark DESC;

parts.label: 6(c)
parts.question: Using an existing MySQLi connection $conn, show the core prepared-statement steps to insert $name and $email into students(name,email).
parts.answer: Prepare placeholders, bind two strings, execute and close.
parts.alternatives: An equivalent PDO prepared statement receives full credit.

parts.label: 7(a)
parts.question: Explain the roles of Model, View and Controller.
parts.answer: Model: data/business data logic. View: presentation. Controller: handles request/input and coordinates model/view.

parts.label: 7(b)
parts.question: State two advantages and two disadvantages of using a framework.
parts.answer: Advantages may include reuse, structure or speed; disadvantages may include learning curve, overhead, dependency, reduced flexibility or framework security risk.

parts.label: 8(a)
parts.question: A mobile client needs a lightweight JSON interface, while a partner requires a strict XML service contract. Recommend REST or SOAP for each and justify each recommendation.
parts.answer: REST for the mobile JSON interface; SOAP for the strict XML contract. Reasons must connect resource-oriented HTTP/lightweight representation and SOAP/WSDL contract/message standards to the scenarios.

parts.label: 9(a)
parts.question: For each case, identify the vulnerability and primary correction: SQL concatenates user input; a comment is printed without encoding; a password is stored as plain text.
parts.answer: SQL injection/prepared statement; XSS/contextual output encoding; password exposure/password_hash plus password_verify.

parts.label: 9(b)
parts.question: State four controls for secure authenticated sessions.
parts.answer: Any four: HTTPS; regenerate ID after login; Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite cookie; no IDs in URLs; inactivity/absolute timeout; destroy on logout; server-side authorisation on every request.
